vt17_jerusalem.topic: The Holy See, partition and the Jerusalem campaign, 1947-1958

claims.text: In multiplicibus curis (24 Oct 1948): Palestine 'occupies a particular place on account of the war which harasses it'; 'thousands of refugees, homeless and driven, wander from their fatherland'; damage to sacred buildings; para. 8 asks for 'an international character which, in the present circumstances, seems to offer a better guarantee' for Jerusalem and free access to holy places 'with international guarantees'; addressed to the 'high quarters' where peace is discussed, not to governments by name.

UNGA res. 303 (IV), 9 Dec 1949, restated intention that Jerusalem be placed under a permanent international regime, as a corpus separatum under a special international regime, with the Trusteeship Council as Administering Authority.

Res. 303 adopted 38-14-7; Arab and Muslim states and the Soviet bloc voted in favour, as did France, Belgium, Australia and several Latin American states; Israel, the US, UK and Canada against; Israel declared Jerusalem its capital in December 1949.

Irish government files released in Dublin (reported by AFP, Jan 2004): Dec 1948 Spain proposed, after a remark by Pius XII, that Catholic states seek a Jerusalem mandate; April 1949 Irish, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese ambassadors met at the Vatican; plan dropped because of 'the reluctance of the Vatican to disclose its hand'; Vatican feared being 'saddled with responsibility'.

Pius XII founded the Pontifical Mission for Palestine in 1949 (June per Wikipedia); in April 1949 he summoned Msgr Thomas J. McMahon, national secretary of CNEWA, and named him president; aim to unify Church relief among refugees; served as the Holy See's liaison with UN agencies.

Tenembaum (2009) recounts that Moshe Shertok feared the Vatican would sway Latin American delegations against partition; Moshe Sneh met Mgr Domenico Tardini on 3 October 1947, arranged by nuncio Roncalli; Tardini 'did not make any promises'; account rests on recollections, no archive cited. Latin American votes: 12 (or 13 incl. Haiti) yes, 6 abstain, Cuba no.

Israel MFA: Sept 1948 Israeli delegation to the Vatican reached 'various understandings'; 1950 Vatican orchestrated an unsuccessful UN internationalization attempt; 1952 Sharett met Pius XII; Jan 1964 visit made 'patently, and painfully, clear that the Holy See did not recognise Israel de jure'; reasons given by MFA: sovereignty over Jerusalem, no recognised borders, holy places, local Catholics, refugees, fear of backlash against Christian minorities in Arab countries.

Wikipedia: Auspicia quaedam 1 May 1948 on holy places; Vatican diplomacy helped place international status for Jerusalem in res. 181; Gori's 1950 offer to Ben-Gurion rejected; 26 May 1955 Israel Philharmonic played without Israel named; Paul VI received Golda Meir 15 Jan 1973 and Dayan 12 Jan 1978; 1967 'special statute, internationally guaranteed'; 29 Jul 1992 commission; nunciature opened 19 Jan 1994; FA in force 10 Mar 1994; Hadas credentials 29 Sep 1994; Legal Personality Agreement 10 Nov 1997; Knesset has not ratified.

Maria Chiara Rioli, 'Archives in War: The Pius XII Papers and the Israeli–Palestinian Conflict', ch. 14 in Unger-Alvi and Valbousquet (eds), Global Pontificate of Pius XII (Berghahn, Aug 2024), pp. 307-324; findings not checked here.

Robson on Rioli's A Liminal Church (2020): based on Latin Patriarchate, Custody, CNEWA archives; after Patriarch Barlassina's death in 1947 the patriarchate had no active head for about two years; Vatican unsure how far to commit; Church's most immediate task was refugees, sometimes advocating their return.

vt17_nostra_notes.topic: Nostra Aetate, the 1974 Guidelines, the 1985 Notes and John Paul II's steps, 1964-1990

claims.text: Evrony: during Paul VI's 1964 visit (an '11-hour-visit' to Israel) he 'did not mention the name Israel'; his thank-you telegram was addressed to 'President Shazar, Tel Aviv'; 1947 the Holy See objected to partition 'on the basis of theological reasons and practical interests'; 1984 first signed papal document to mention the 'State of Israel'.

Paul VI's pilgrimage 4-6 January 1964: flew to Amman, received by King Hussein; entered Israel at Megiddo on 5 January, greeted by President Zalman Shazar and PM Levi Eshkol; met Patriarch Athenagoras in Jerusalem; Mass in Bethlehem 6 January.
JTA 24 Dec 1963: Chief Rabbi Yitzhak Nissim would not take part in welcoming ceremonies at Megiddo or the Mandelbaum Gate, his participation possible only 'on the basis of reciprocity'.

Fumagalli: John XXIII met Jules Isaac on 13 June 1960; outline on Jews removed from agenda June 1962; final vote 28 October 1965, 2,221 to 88; promulgated; repudiated collective and permanent responsibility for the death of Christ.

Rutishauser: in the first session the 'Wardi Affair' prevented the text being presented: the WJC named Dr Chaim Wardi, an official of Israel's Ministry of Religious Affairs, as its observer; Arab governments protested; Wardi never attended; Arab states' representatives saw the draft as 'a Zionist conspiracy'; vote 28 Oct 1965 2221-88.

Guidelines dated 1 December 1974, signed by Cardinal Willebrands (President) and Pierre-Marie de Contenson OP (Secretary); 'On 22 October 1974, the Holy Father instituted for the universal Church this Commission'; Christians must learn 'by what essential traits the Jews define themselves in the light of their own religious experience'; the document does not address the land or State of Israel.

Redemptionis anno, 20 April 1984: 'For the Jewish people who live in the State of Israel ... we must ask for the desired security and the due tranquility'; Palestinians 'have the natural right in justice to find once more a homeland'; Jerusalem by 'a special statute internationally guaranteed'.
John Paul II visited Rome's synagogue on 13 April 1986, welcomed by Chief Rabbi Elio Toaff: 'You are our dearly beloved brothers', 'our elder brothers'.

Arafat audience with John Paul II, 15 Sept 1982: Begin criticized the pope and accused the Vatican of inactivity during the Holocaust; an Israeli official said Israel was 'very disturbed'; the Vatican 'angrily rejected Israel's charges'.

June 1987: Shamir called the pope's planned audience for Austrian president Kurt Waldheim an 'unfriendly act'; without relations Israel 'can do nothing but express its unhappiness'; the Vatican said it was 'surprised and profoundly grieved'.
Vatican statement of 20 June 1987 defended the Waldheim meeting as a state visit by a democratically elected head of state; Navarro-Valls said Austria had 'repeatedly requested' it.
After a 1 Sept 1987 meeting with Jewish leaders the Vatican agreed to prepare a document on the Holocaust and to give further consideration to diplomatic relations with Israel.

vt17_fundamental_agreement.topic: Madrid, Oslo and the Fundamental Agreement, 1991-1994

claims.text: AP 30 Dec 1993: Beilin and Mgr Claudio Celli, Vatican undersecretary for relations with states, signed at Israel's Foreign Ministry in Jerusalem; a Vatican statement sought an internationally guaranteed 'special status' for Jerusalem and freedom of worship and access; the Vatican had resisted recognition since 1948 citing treatment of Palestinians, church property and Jerusalem; two years to negotiate property and economic issues; about 80 religious Israelis protested; a Syrian Orthodox Christian said it was 'against the Palestinian people'; Patriarch Michel Sabbah tied it to the 'general process of reconciliation'.

Rosen: Holy See spokespersons attributed the delay to political, not theological, considerations ('secular political considerations'); Church feared backlash in Arab and Muslim societies; local Palestinian Catholic leadership opposed advances 'until Palestinian political claims had been satisfied'; turning point the Permanent Bilateral Commission, July 1992; Holy See sought de jure what it had de facto (legal status, education, taxation); Navarro-Valls: 'The Palestinians are talking with Israelis, why shouldn't we?' and relations 'the culmination of a process'; quotes Gasparri 1919: 'the danger that frightens us the most, is that of the creation of a Jewish State in Palestine'.

Madrid Conference opened 30 October 1991 (to 4 Nov), co-chaired by Bush and Gorbachev, with Israeli, Egyptian, Syrian, Lebanese and joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegations; direct Israel-PLO talks culminated in the Declaration of Principles of 13 September 1993.
Oslo I signed at a public ceremony in Washington, 13 September 1993, with Letters of Mutual Recognition.
